items.title: No Relief for Mortgage Rates as August Jobs Report Comes in Hot
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Any hope of a trend reversal for mortgage rates seems to be DOA. A cooler-than-expected jobs report this morning could have taken the pressure off. But instead, it came in well above expectations, piling even more pain onto interest rates. It also increased the odds of a September Fed rate hike to over 60%. Perhaps… Read More »

items.title: Why Mortgage Rates Are Near a One-Year High
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: While they aren’t at their absolute worst, mortgage rates remain very close to their one-year high. They’re about .125% below their 52-week highs, which were seen in late July before we got some favorable economic data. However, they remain stubbornly high with no real relief in sight. items.title: Is AI Pushing Mortgage Rates Higher?
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: A lot of the recent uptick in mortgage rates has been attributed to the ongoing war with Iran. But there is perhaps another, lesser known reason mortgage rates have pushed back into the high 6s. And it’s all the artificial intelligence (AI) spending, which has arguably crowded out other investments, leading to higher bond yields.… Read More »

items.title: Mortgage Rates Simply Trying to Limit the Damage Right Now
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: The best way to sum up mortgage rates right now is any “good news” is simply stopping the bleeding. You’re not seeing sizable drops when positive stuff happens.
